findings.where: Whole page at desktop width: the single text column against the content area set by the nav
findings.fault: All the content sits in one narrow column, about 520 px wide, pinned to the left edge of a 1050 px content area. The right 60% of every screen is empty sand from the hero to the footer, and nothing fills it: no contents list, no summary panel, no figure. The nav's right-hand links mark out a wide frame that the body never uses, so the page looks lopsided, as if a sidebar failed to load.
findings.who_objects: A visitor on a laptop who came to check whether the ranking can be trusted. On a page whose job is trust, a layout that looks half-rendered suggests the method was put up in a hurry.

findings.where: Intro, the three numbered commitments under the lead paragraph
findings.fault: The three promises a visitor came for (no paid position, recent stays count more, few reviews start near the area average) are set as a plain small list. They are smaller and quieter than the lead paragraph above them, with no grouping or emphasis. In a squint, the h1 and the lead win and the commitments look like a footnote. The lead talks about publishing the method, while the actual answer sits below it at body size.
findings.who_objects: A backpacker skimming on a phone to answer 'can hostels pay to rank higher?' Their eye stops at the large lead paragraph and may skip the list that answers the question.

findings.where: Ranking method section: its four long paragraphs (payment, pull toward the area average, which reviews count and badges, review count and zero reviews)
findings.fault: Four separate topics run as one unbroken block of long paragraphs under a single heading, with no subheads, lead sentences set apart or other breaks. On the phone this is about a screen and a half of even grey text. On desktop it fills most of two screens, while the other sections are short, so the page's rhythm is lopsided.
findings.who_objects: A visitor who wants one specific answer, such as what 'No reviews yet' means or whether a badge means a confirmed stay. They have to read the whole block to find it, on a phone, often while in transit.

findings.where: Footer link row at phone width
findings.fault: The link row wraps after 'How we rank' and leaves a stray '·' separator dangling at the end of the first line. The second line ('Report content · email') then starts with no separator, so the two lines look like two different groups.
findings.who_objects: A careful reader on a phone reaching the contact and report links. It looks unfinished, but few will notice.
